final_recommendation: The room converged on a fully operationalized risk calendar with concrete triggers: Jan 15 OEM capex commitment gate, March 31 CPTPP filing deadline, May 31 Commerce re-determination tariff trigger, and named supplier insolvency pricing for five plants (two Monterrey fastener shops, Saltillo stamping operations). Ford F-Series platform exposure quantified at $1.2M-$2.8M capex per plant, with 75-day stranded AR reserve and 40% enforcement-uncertainty premium priced into trade-credit and political-risk underwriting.
minority_objections: Supply-chain consultant initially pushed for pre-screening all 12 plants in November rather than waiting for Dec 15 audit, but was overruled by CFO's decision to triage only the five highest-risk plants
Auto-strategy questioned whether the Jan 15 commitment gate was a 'coin flip' rather than a decision rule, but CFO locked the gate with explicit insolvency-pricing trigger
key_conflicts: Whether to absorb supplier re-qualification capex across the board (auto-strategy's 'margin kill' objection) versus cost-share tied to volume commitments
Whether to wait for Dec 15 audit results or pre-screen plants in November (supplier versus CFO)
Whether tariff penalty triggers on March 31 filing day or May 31 Commerce re-determination (compliance lawyer versus political-risk insurer, resolved as May 31 actual penalty trigger)
key_concessions: CFO conceded that Monterrey shops are already priced at insolvency rates if capex doesn't land by Jan 15, not waiting for audit failure
Political-risk insurer accepted March 31 filing-day exposure as the pricing anchor despite May 31 being the actual penalty trigger
Auto-strategy accepted that Ford runs their own RVC audit lab, removing third-party cert uncertainty
Trade-credit underwriter accepted Ford's net-30 contractual lock through March 31, but priced 75-day stranded AR window for post-audit failures
red_lines: Jan 15 OEM capex commitment deadline: if not met, insolvency pricing activates immediately
March 31 CPTPP filing deadline: RVC recounts must hit docket or tariffs apply retroactively to in-transit inventory
Ford F-Series platform cannot lose RVC certification on 40% of sub-assemblies without triggering business interruption exposure
No absorption of re-qualification capex across the board without volume-commitment cost-share
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Broader supplier base beyond the five named plants: the room focused exclusively on Monterrey fasteners and Saltillo stamping, leaving other tier-2 suppliers unpriced
Labor-content wage-floor compliance mechanics: the 8-point and 12-point labor-content gaps were quantified but not translated into ongoing wage-monitoring or enforcement triggers
CPTPP versus USMCA filing pathway choice: the room locked March 31 CPTPP deadline but did not explore whether Commerce re-determination could shift the compliance pathway
Business interruption insurance pricing: mentioned as exposure on F-Series platform but not operationalized into premium structure or coverage limits
downstream_risk_variables: Stranded accounts receivable: $340K reserve held against 75-day payment freeze if Monterrey fails audit
Tariff exposure on in-transit inventory: retroactive application if March 31 filing missed
Supplier insolvency cascade: if two Monterrey fastener shops fail, diversified Saltillo stamping operations may face liquidity pressure from OEM payment-term freezes
Texas nearshoring transition cost: mentioned as OEM absorption if Monterrey doesn't commit, but lead time and Dallas supplier capacity not quantified
2026 USMCA sunset review shock premium: 25% conditional premium if Hill moves on RVC mid-cycle, priced against post-May 31 enforcement
uncertainty_notes: The room did not resolve: (1) which specific Texas plant is the named nearshoring alternative for Monterrey fasteners, or its lead time; (2) whether Ford's 45-day audit window commitment is contractual or aspirational; (3) how the 40% enforcement-uncertainty threshold is measured or triggered in real-time; (4) whether the $340K stranded AR reserve is adequate if multiple suppliers fail simultaneously; (5) business interruption coverage limits or premium structure for F-Series platform exposure.

marker_evidence.rules_of_origin_burden: Fully operationalized: $1.2M Monterrey and $2.8M Saltillo RVC recount costs quantified per plant, 62% vs 75% RVC shortfall specified, March 31 CPTPP filing deadline locked as compliance trigger, Ford audit ownership named
marker_evidence.labor_cost_pressure: Quantified but not operationalized: 8-point and 12-point labor-content gaps versus wage floor identified, but no ongoing wage-monitoring trigger, enforcement mechanism, or premium structure tied to labor compliance
marker_evidence.supplier_relocation_pressure: Fully operationalized: five plants named (two Monterrey fastener, Saltillo stamping), Jan 15 capex commitment gate triggers insolvency pricing, 18-24 month re-qual cycles specified, 85% Ford customer concentration quantified, Texas nearshoring option named as decision alternative
marker_evidence.nearshoring_incentive: Concrete but not fully operationalized: Texas nearshoring presented as decision alternative to Monterrey failure, Dallas supplier mentioned, but lead time and capacity not quantified, transition cost assigned to OEM but not priced into underwriting model
marker_evidence.trade_credit_stress: Fully operationalized: $340K stranded AR reserve locked, 75-day payment freeze window tied to Jan 15 gate and May 31 re-determination, Ford net-30 contractual lock through March 31 specified, insolvency pricing activates Jan 16 if capex fails
marker_evidence.political_risk_score: Fully operationalized: 40% enforcement-uncertainty threshold activates 15% premium, March 31 filing-day exposure priced despite May 31 actual penalty trigger, 25% conditional shock premium on 2026 USMCA review, Commerce re-determination velocity named as enforcement-certainty anchor
marker_evidence.business_interruption_exposure: Identified but not operationalized: F-Series platform 40% sub-assembly exposure quantified, business interruption mentioned as consequence of Monterrey failure, but no premium structure, coverage limits, or contingent-BI trigger defined
